channels.research: Note the 'wwws' subdomain — this is not a typo, and www.airfrance.fr is not the same host. Reached via the official EC261 passenger-rights notice at https://wwws.airfrance.fr/information/legal/assistance-et-indemnisation, which links this exact URL under 'Compléter le formulaire'. That notice also states compensation cannot be paid at the airport and must go through customer service, and that claims must be addressed to the OPERATING carrier — relevant for AF/KL codeshares. AF offers a choice between a non-refundable travel voucher (350/500/800 EUR) and cash (250/400/600 EUR); the voucher is the higher headline number and is likely what the airline steers claimants toward. Notice last updated September 2024.

CRITICAL IF YOU SUBMIT ON SOMEONE ELSE'S BEHALF: Ryanair operates a mandatory registration scheme for Claims Management Companies and has litigated successfully (UK County Court, upheld jurisdiction clause) to force claims through its own channel rather than third parties. Its terms require claims be submitted directly by the passenger. An automated tool acting as an intermediary is squarely in the category Ryanair is set up to block — this is why thirdPartySubmission is 'restricted', which also forces autoSendChannel to null.

channels.research: Best-documented carrier in this file. The same endpoint handles compensation, expense reimbursement, downgrade refunds and denied-boarding claims — the claim type is selected inside the form, so one URL covers four cases. BA warns the flow takes 10-15 minutes. Third-party claims require a signed letter of authority from every passenger included, and BA separately requires authorisation where surnames differ within one booking. BA quotes both EUR and GBP amounts (250/400/600 EUR or 220/350/520 GBP) — post-Brexit this is UK261 for UK departures and EU261 otherwise, and BA runs them through the same channel. A claim-status checker lives at /content/information/help-and-contacts/complaints-and-claims. An expenses-only shortcut also exists at /travel/helpcentre/?dt=1|1|1&id=2.

channels.research: Previously marked unsupported because turkishairlines.com timed out — it does resolve, but the customer-relations path 302s to a separate subdomain, feedback.turkishairlines.com, which is what was actually timing out under the old host. Allowlist both. There is NO dedicated EC261 form: compensation is requested through the general feedback portal by selecting the flight-disruption category and supplying the EU departure airport plus delay length or cancellation details. The portal issues a case reference (observed format TK-XXXXXXX) usable for tracking. Requires the 6-character PNR. Coverage caveat: TK is a non-EU carrier, so EC261 applies only to EU departures — an IST-JFK flight is out of scope, a FRA-IST flight is in scope. That is already enforced by isEuCarrier plus domain/ec261/eligibility.ts, not by this entry.
